intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with the whole family. Hanauma Bay offers calm, clear waters teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles, making it perfect for beginner and experienced snorkelers alike. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner Experience at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring an imu ceremony (underground pig roast), hula dancing performances, fire knife dancing, and a lavish buffet of local Hawaiian dishes including poi, kalua pork, lomi salmon, and haupia coconut pudding. A memorable cultural evening for all ages.

experiences.name: Waimea Valley Nature Walk and Waterfall Swim
experiences.description: Hike through a lush botanical garden along a well-maintained family-friendly trail leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Kids and adults can swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall (life jackets provided). The valley also features cultural demonstrations and ancient Hawaiian archaeological sites along the path.

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium Visit
experiences.description: Discover Hawaii's incredible marine life at one of the finest aquariums in the United States. Walk through an underwater tunnel surrounded by sharks, rays, and hundreds of tropical fish species. The center features interactive tide pools, turtle exhibits, and whale discovery centers that educate and entertain children and adults alike. A perfect rainy-day or mid-day activity.

experiences.name: Kailua Beach Kayaking and Sandbar Adventure
experiences.description: Paddle across the crystal-clear turquoise waters of Kailua Bay to the famous Flat Island sandbar and Popoia Island. Rent kayaks or join a guided family tour and enjoy one of Oahu's most beautiful and uncrowded beaches. The calm bay conditions make it ideal for children, and the white sand beach is perfect for building sandcastles and picnicking after your paddle.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30 via Flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation (TheBus route 20 or 42 is the most budget-friendly option at ~$3 per ride), and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Do a quick orientation of the hotel and nearby surroundings.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport before baggage claim or pick up snacks from a 24-hour ABC Store near the hotel (~$5-10)

day_by_day.notes: Since arrival is at 22:30, no activities are planned for this day. Rest well — a full adventure begins tomorrow! Pick up a bus pass or grab a map from the hotel lobby to plan transportation for the week.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a leisurely walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. If the hotel is near Waikiki, stroll along Waikiki Beach (free) and watch the early morning surfers. Collect shells with the kids and enjoy the sunrise over Diamond Head.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kapiolani Regional Park (free entry) — a massive open green space adjacent to Waikiki Beach, perfect for families. Bring a frisbee or ball. Walk the paved paths, spot peacocks, and enjoy the ocean breeze. Alternatively, rent a boogie board from a local beach stand (~$10/hour) and hit the gentle Waikiki waves.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Royal Hawaiian Center for the free weekly hula show (check schedule, usually evenings). Enjoy the open-air atmosphere and free cultural entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh fruit and a plate lunch from a local farmers market stall or ABC Store (~$6-8 per person)
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In — a Honolulu institution. Try the mixed plate for ~$10-12. Family-friendly and casual.
meals.dinner: Musubi Cafe Iyasume near Waikiki for spam musubi and affordable Hawaiian staples (~$8-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a 7-day bus pass (HOLO card) at a participating retailer for ~$35 — it pays for itself quickly and is the best budget transport option on Oahu.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — one of Hawaii's most stunning snorkeling spots. Arrive early (opens at 6:45 AM) to beat the crowds. Entry is $25/adult, children under 12 free. Snorkel gear rental is available on-site (~$15). Watch the mandatory marine education video before entering the bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, head to nearby Sandy Beach Park (free) — great for bodyboarding and watching experienced surfers tackle powerful shore break. Families with younger kids can relax on the sand while older kids watch the action.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area and walk Kalakaua Avenue in Waikiki. Browse the free International Market Place outdoor areas and enjoy the street performers and ambient Hawaiian music.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from the hotel or grab a quick bite at a nearby convenience store before heading out (~$5)
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch or purchase from the snack bar at Hanauma Bay (~$8-12)
meals.dinner: Eggs 'n Things on Kalakaua Avenue — famous for pancakes and local-style breakfast-for-dinner. Budget ~$12-15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online (book at least 2 days ahead). The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Bring reef-safe sunscreen — it's required and enforced at the bay.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument — a short bus ride from Waikiki. The hike to the summit is about 1.6 miles round trip and takes 1.5-2 hours. Entry is $5/person or $10/car. The panoramic views of Honolulu and the Pacific are spectacular and well worth the effort. Suitable for older kids and active families.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, cool off at Ala Moana Beach Park (free) — a calm, protected beach ideal for families with young children. The water is gentle and shallow. Enjoy the wide sandy shores and shaded picnic areas.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's largest open-air shopping mall. Window shop, enjoy free entertainment, and grab affordable food court options. Check if there are free hula or live music performances scheduled.

meals.breakfast: Liliha Bakery — a beloved local institution. Try the coco puffs and local breakfast plates (~$8-12 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks for the Diamond Head hike to save money (~$5-8)
meals.dinner: Ala Moana Center Food Court — wide variety of local options including poke bowls, plate lunches, and Asian cuisine (~$10-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start Diamond Head early (before 8 AM if possible) to avoid midday heat and crowds. Bring plenty of water for the hike — at least 1 liter per person. Wear closed-toe shoes for the rocky trail.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided walking tour of historic Chinatown in downtown Honolulu. Explore colorful lei shops, open-air markets, local bakeries, and cultural murals. Visit the Oahu Market (one of Hawaii's oldest markets) and the Foster Botanical Garden (~$5 adult, free for kids under 12).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Iolani Palace (the only royal palace in the US) — guided tours are available for ~$27/adult, $7/child, or opt for the self-guided audio tour at ~$20/adult. This is a great educational experience for families interested in Hawaiian history and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the free Sunset on the Beach event on Waikiki Beach (check local schedule — typically held on weekends). Enjoy movies on a giant inflatable screen with the ocean as your backdrop. Bring a blanket and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Explore Chinatown's local bakeries for char siu bao (steamed buns), malasadas, or dim sum (~$4-7 per person)
meals.lunch: Maunakea Marketplace Food Court in Chinatown — authentic and very affordable local food from multiple vendors (~$8-10 per person)
meals.dinner: Pick up plate lunches or poke bowls from a local grocery deli (Times Supermarket or Foodland) for a budget beach picnic (~$8-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Chinatown is best explored in the morning when markets are freshest and most active. Keep an eye on belongings in busy market areas. Iolani Palace is closed on Sundays and Mondays — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant experience. The USS Arizona Memorial is free (reserve tickets online in advance at recreation.gov). The visitor center and exhibits are also free. Budget 3-4 hours for the full experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Pearl Harbor, stop by the USS Bowfin Submarine Museum & Park (~$15/adult, $8/child) adjacent to the Pearl Harbor site. Kids love exploring the submarine. Alternatively, visit the nearby Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum (~$25/adult, $15/child) if budget allows.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki and enjoy a relaxing evening beach walk. Watch the famous Waikiki sunset — one of the best free shows in Hawaii. Many local musicians play on the beach in the evenings.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at McDonald's for budget-friendly morning fuel (~$6-8)
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor has a cafeteria on site, or bring packed sandwiches (~$8-12)
meals.dinner: Ono Hawaiian Foods in Honolulu — authentic Hawaiian comfort food (lau lau, poi, kalua pig) at very reasonable prices (~$12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor timed entry passes for the Arizona Memorial boat tour book up weeks in advance — reserve online as soon as possible. No bags larger than a small purse are allowed at the memorial; use the paid storage lockers on site ($5).

day_by_day.morning: Explore the North Shore of Oahu — take TheBus Route 60 (about 2 hours) or consider renting a car for the day (~$50-70) to maximize time. Visit Sunset Beach and Banzai Pipeline, two of the world's most famous surf spots. In August, waves are typically calm and ideal for swimming and snorkeling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Waimea Bay Beach Park — a stunning crescent-shaped bay with calm summer waters. Jump from the famous Waimea Rock (a local tradition). Explore the adjacent Waimea Valley (~$20/adult, $10/child) for botanical gardens and a freshwater waterfall swim.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Haleiwa Town — the charming surf town on the North Shore. Browse local art galleries, surf shops, and enjoy the laid-back aloha vibe. Watch the sunset over the harbor before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa — the original and most famous shrimp truck in Hawaii. Garlic shrimp plate is ~$14-16 and worth every penny.
meals.lunch: Matsumoto Shave Ice in Haleiwa — a legendary North Shore institution. Shave ice from ~$4-6. Perfect afternoon treat.
meals.dinner: Kono's Northshore in Haleiwa for affordable burritos and local-style wraps (~$10-13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is about 35 miles from Waikiki. If using TheBus, leave early as the journey takes approximately 2 hours each way. Renting a car for this day makes the most sense logistically. Check surf conditions — in August, North Shore is typically calm and safe for families.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie (~1 hour from Waikiki by bus). This is one of Hawaii's most popular family attractions. The daytime village admission is ~$60/adult and $48/child — a splurge but worth it for families. Explore six Pacific island villages, watch cultural demonstrations, and participate in hands-on activities like coconut husking and hula lessons.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — catch the canoe pageant on the waterway (included with admission) and watch live cultural performances throughout the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel and enjoy a quiet evening. Take a final sunset stroll along Waikiki Beach and pick up any souvenirs from local shops or ABC Stores (most affordable souvenir option in Hawaii).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab pastries from a nearby bakery (~$6-8)
meals.lunch: The Gateway Buffet at Polynesian Cultural Center is included in some ticket packages — check when booking. Otherwise, food is available on-site (~$15-20)
meals.dinner: Kapahulu Avenue — known as Honolulu's 'local food row.' Try Ono Seafood for poke bowls (~$12-15) or Helena's Hawaiian Food for traditional Hawaiian plates (~$15-18)

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is the most expensive day of the trip but is highly recommended for families. Look for discount tickets through Costco or the hotel concierge. The evening show (Ha: Breath of Life) costs extra (~$20-30 more) — optional but spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final full morning at the beach — try a new stretch of Waikiki or head to Kailua Beach on the Windward side (rated one of America's best beaches). Kailua is about 30 minutes by car or 1 hour by bus. The calm, turquoise water and white sand are ideal for families. Rent kayaks (~$25/hour for a double) to paddle out to the Mokulua Islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Byodo-In Temple in the Valley of the Temples Memorial Park in Kaneohe (~$5/person). This stunning replica of a 900-year-old Japanese temple sits against dramatic green cliffs. Feed the koi fish and peacocks — kids absolutely love it.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a final evening dinner. Walk along the beach one last time and enjoy the warm Hawaiian night. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs and pack for tomorrow's departure.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — famous for guava chiffon pancakes and local breakfast (~$12-15 per person)
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua — a beloved local deli with fresh sandwiches, salads, and snacks (~$10-13 per person)
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki — a classic Waikiki beachfront restaurant with happy hour deals and a festive atmosphere. Budget ~$20-25 per person for a special farewell dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach has no lifeguards — supervise children carefully. The beach has no food vendors, so bring snacks and water. Byodo-In Temple is a peaceful, photogenic stop that pairs well with the Windward side day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely morning in Hawaii. Take one last walk on the beach at sunrise. Swim, collect a few shells as keepsakes, and soak in the aloha spirit. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout is typically 11 AM — confirm with hotel).
day_by_day.afternoon: If your flight is in the afternoon or evening, store luggage at the hotel and spend remaining time at Waikiki Beach or browse the International Market Place. Visit the free Honolulu Zoo entrance area or stroll through Kapiolani Park one final time.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport. Allow at least 2-3 hours before departure for check-in and security. TheBus Route 20 runs to the airport from Waikiki (~$3, about 45 minutes).

meals.breakfast: Splurge on a final local breakfast at Wailana Coffee House — open 24 hours, classic diner-style Hawaiian breakfast (~$10-14 per person)
meals.lunch: Grab a final poke bowl or plate lunch from a local spot near Waikiki (~$10-13)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or pack snacks for the flight to save money (~$10-15)

day_by_day.notes: Mahalo for an amazing trip! Use any remaining cash on local snacks or small souvenirs at the airport. Consider picking up Hawaiian coffee, macadamia nuts, or local chocolates as affordable gifts. TheBus to the airport is the most budget-friendly option — allow extra time as buses run every 20-30 minutes.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation (pre-booked shuttle or rideshare ~$30-40), and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront. Unwind with a welcome drink at the resort bar if still open.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the departure airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the departure airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night bite at the resort's lobby café or a nearby 24-hour spot like Zippy's (local Hawaii comfort food chain, ~$10-15)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — arrival is late at night. Lay out essentials, set an alarm, and get a good night's rest to start fresh tomorrow. Confirm resort check-in details in advance since arrival is after 10 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Take a relaxed first walk along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the ocean and explore the resort amenities — pool, beach chairs, and ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kailua Beach (approx. 30-45 min drive or arrange resort shuttle) for the Kailua Beach Kayaking and Sandbar Adventure. Paddle across the crystal-clear turquoise waters of Kailua Bay to the famous Flat Island sandbar — a perfect family-friendly introduction to Hawaii's stunning coastline. Rentals available on-site (~$60-80 for a double kayak).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and freshen up. Stroll along the beachfront promenade and enjoy the sunset. Head to a nearby casual restaurant for a relaxed family dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet or café (~$15-20/person)
meals.lunch: Kailua Town stop — Kalapawai Café & Deli for fresh sandwiches, salads, and local plates (~$12-18/person)
meals.dinner: Buzz's Original Steak House in Kailua — a local institution with great steaks, seafood, and a relaxed vibe (~$25-40/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kailua kayaking experience in advance, especially in August (peak season). Apply reef-safe sunscreen — it's required at many Hawaii beaches. Bring water shoes for the sandbar.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries. Arrive by 7:00-7:30 AM to secure parking and entry (reservations required online, ~$25/adult, free for children under 12). Watch the mandatory marine education video before entering the bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive along the scenic Kalanianaole Highway (Hwy 72) — the southeastern coastline route. Stop at Halona Blowhole and Sandy Beach for photos and a stretch. Return to the resort for a pool afternoon and relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset dinner at a beachfront restaurant near the resort. Let the kids wind down with a beach bonfire (if permitted by resort) or evening swim in the resort pool.

meals.breakfast: Early and light before Hanauma Bay — grab granola bars and fruit from a convenience store or resort grab-and-go
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Hanauma Bay (bring your own snacks and sandwiches — outside food is allowed) or grab shave ice at a roadside stand on the way back (~$5-8)
meals.dinner: Roy's Hawaii Kai — celebrated chef Roy Yamaguchi's flagship restaurant with Hawaiian Fusion cuisine (~$35-55/person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations must be made online in advance — slots fill up weeks ahead in August. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Bring your own snorkel gear or rent on-site (~$12). No touching the coral or marine life.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial for a moving and educational family experience. Tour the USS Arizona Memorial, USS Bowfin Submarine, and Battleship Missouri. Allow 3-4 hours minimum. Book tickets online in advance (USS Arizona boat tour ~$1, other attractions $25-30/person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to downtown Honolulu's Chinatown and Aloha Tower Marketplace for a leisurely afternoon stroll. Browse local shops, pick up souvenirs, and enjoy the harbor views. Visit the Aloha Tower observation deck for panoramic city and ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Waikiki Beach for the classic Hawaii evening experience. Walk the famous strip, watch hula performers, and enjoy the vibrant energy. End with dinner in Waikiki.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Pho To Chau in Chinatown — authentic Vietnamese pho and local favorites at great value (~$10-14/person)
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki — iconic oceanfront restaurant named after Duke Kahanamoku with great seafood, burgers, and live music (~$25-40/person)

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is a solemn memorial — remind children to be respectful. Arrive early as lines get long. The USS Arizona boat tour is free but requires timed-entry tickets reserved online. Bags must be stored in paid lockers on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the North Shore of Oahu — a scenic 45-60 minute drive from the resort. Visit Waimea Valley for the Waimea Valley Nature Walk and Waterfall Swim. Hike through a lush botanical garden on a well-maintained family-friendly trail leading to a stunning 45-foot waterfall with a swimming hole (~$20/adult, $10/child).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the North Shore to Haleiwa Town — the charming surf town hub. Browse local boutiques, art galleries, and surf shops. Stop at the famous Matsumoto Shave Ice for a classic Hawaii treat.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Sunset Beach or Ehukai Beach (Banzai Pipeline) — iconic surf spots with dramatic scenery. Return to the resort for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast on the way — Cinnamon's at the Ilikai in Honolulu or a local bakery stop (~$12-18/person)
meals.lunch: Haleiwa Joe's Seafood Grill — casual North Shore dining with fresh seafood and gorgeous garden views (~$18-28/person)
meals.dinner: Back near the resort — Kona Brewing Company for craft beers, pizza, and pub fare in a casual family-friendly setting (~$18-25/person)

day_by_day.notes: Life jackets are provided at Waimea Valley waterfall — swimming is allowed when conditions are safe. August is summer in Hawaii so North Shore waves are typically calm (large surf season is winter). Bring cash for Matsumoto Shave Ice — card not always accepted.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Maui — take an inter-island flight (Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest, ~$80-120/person, 30-minute flight). Check in to the Maui extension of your accommodations or a comparable beachfront hotel in Lahaina or Kaanapali area. Drop bags and head straight to the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Maui Ocean Center Aquarium in Maalaea — one of the finest aquariums in the United States. Walk through an open-ocean tunnel surrounded by sharks, rays, and thousands of tropical fish. Perfect for the whole family (~$35/adult, $25/child). Allow 2-3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Lahaina Town for a classic Maui evening. Stroll Front Street, browse galleries, and admire the famous 150-year-old Banyan Tree in Banyan Tree Park. Enjoy dinner in Lahaina.

meals.breakfast: Quick bite at Honolulu Airport before the flight — Island Brew Coffeehouse or ABC Store grab-and-go
meals.lunch: Maui Ocean Center has a café on-site (Beach Bento) — convenient and reasonably priced (~$12-16/person)
meals.dinner: Lahaina Fish Company — open-air oceanfront dining with fresh fish, sushi, and classic Hawaiian plates right on the water (~$25-40/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights 2-3 weeks in advance for best prices. Confirm whether your resort package includes Maui accommodations or if you need to book separately. Maui Ocean Center is closed on certain holidays — verify hours online.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the legendary Road to Hana — one of the world's most scenic coastal drives. Start early (7:00 AM) to beat traffic. Stop at Twin Falls, Garden of Eden Arboretum, and Wailua Falls. The full drive is 64 miles with 620 curves and 59 bridges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana, stopping at Waianapanapa State Park (Black Sand Beach) — reserve entry online in advance (~$5/person parking + $5/person entry). Swim in the black volcanic sand beach and explore the sea caves. End your drive at Hana Town for a rest.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive along the northern route or take the southern loop back (if renting a car with off-road clearance). Arrive back at Lahaina/Kaanapali for dinner and a well-deserved rest.

meals.breakfast: Pack a cooler with breakfast items from a local grocery store the night before — eat at Twin Falls picnic area
meals.lunch: Roadside food stands along the Road to Hana — try fresh banana bread at Aunty Sandy's (~$5-8) and fruit stands
meals.dinner: Hula Grill Kaanapali — beachfront casual dining with Hawaiian-inspired seafood and great sunset views (~$25-40/person)

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana requires a full day — start early and pace yourselves. Rent a car for this day (compact or SUV, ~$60-90/day). Waianapanapa State Park requires advance reservations online. Bring motion sickness remedies if needed for the winding roads. Fuel up in Paia before starting.

day_by_day.morning: Attend the Old Lahaina Luau — one of Hawaii's most authentic and celebrated luau experiences. Note: Old Lahaina Luau typically runs as an evening event, so spend the morning at Kaanapali Beach. Snorkel at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) — a famous free snorkeling spot right on Kaanapali Beach with sea turtles and tropical fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Lahaina Historic Trail — a self-guided walking tour through Lahaina's rich whaling and missionary history. Visit the Baldwin Home Museum and Lahaina Courthouse. Relax at the resort pool and prepare for the evening luau.
day_by_day.evening: Old Lahaina Luau Dinner Experience — immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional imu ceremony (underground pig roast), hula performances, fire dancing, and a generous buffet of Hawaiian cuisine. One of the most memorable experiences in Hawaii (~$130-160/adult, ~$90/child). Book months in advance.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local café — Gazebo Restaurant in Napili for famous macadamia nut pancakes (~$12-18/person)
meals.lunch: Cool Cat Café in Lahaina — casual 1950s diner-style burgers, wraps, and milkshakes on the second floor overlooking Front Street (~$14-20/person)
meals.dinner: Included in the Old Lahaina Luau experience — extensive Hawaiian buffet with kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia, and more

day_by_day.notes: Old Lahaina Luau is one of the most sought-after experiences in Maui — book 2-3 months in advance as it sells out quickly. The event typically starts at sunset (~5:30-6:00 PM). Dress in aloha attire. The luau is outdoors so bring a light layer for the evening breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive to Haleakala National Park to witness the sunrise from the summit (10,023 feet). Reserve a sunrise permit online in advance (~$1/vehicle reservation fee + $30/vehicle park entry). Arrive at the summit before dawn for a breathtaking, otherworldly experience above the clouds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Haleakala and stop in Upcountry Maui — visit Surfing Goat Dairy or Ali'i Kula Lavender Farm for a fun family detour. Drive back down to the coast and spend the afternoon at Wailea Beach — one of Maui's most beautiful and calm family-friendly beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Final Maui evening — enjoy a sunset dinner at a Wailea resort restaurant. Reflect on the trip and let the kids splash in the warm evening ocean one last time.

meals.breakfast: Pack hot coffee and pastries in a thermos for the Haleakala sunrise (it's cold at the summit — around 40°F)
meals.lunch: Upcountry stop — Grandma's Coffee House in Keokea for homemade soups, sandwiches, and fresh-brewed Maui coffee (~$10-15/person)
meals.dinner: Monkeypod Kitchen in Wailea — farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine with craft cocktails, wood-fired pizzas, and live music (~$25-40/person)

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala sunrise reservations are released 60 days in advance at recreation.gov and sell out within minutes — set an alarm and be ready. Dress in warm layers (40-50°F at summit). The descent back takes about 1.5 hours. Wailea Beach has calm, protected waters ideal for young children.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a slow, relaxed breakfast at the resort. Take one last walk on the beach, collect any final shells or memories, and let the kids have a final swim. Begin packing and check out of accommodations (standard checkout 11:00 AM — confirm with resort).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, visit a nearby local market or shop for last-minute souvenirs and gifts. Maui Swap Meet (if Saturday) or Lahaina shops are great options. Head to Kahului Airport (OGG) for your inter-island connection back to Honolulu (if needed) and onward flight home.
day_by_day.evening: Travel home with wonderful memories of 10 days in Hawaii. Enjoy a final airport meal at the Honolulu Airport's local food options.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a special final meal — Café des Amis in Paia for crepes and Mediterranean fare (~$12-18/person)
meals.lunch: Light and easy — airport food court or a quick stop at Maui's Whole Foods or Safeway for local snacks and macadamia nut treats to bring home
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Honolulu International Airport — Makai Market Food Court or a sit-down option depending on layover time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and allow extra time for airport security — Kahului Airport can be busy in August. Pack reef-safe sunscreen, macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and local jams as great take-home gifts. Inter-island connection to Honolulu typically takes 30 minutes — allow 2.5 hours total for connections.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with the whole family. Hanauma Bay offers calm, clear waters teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles, making it perfect for beginner and experienced snorkelers alike. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner Experience at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring an imu ceremony (underground pig roast), hula dancing performances, fire knife dancing, and a lavish buffet of local Hawaiian dishes including poi, kalua pork, lomi salmon, and haupia coconut pudding. A memorable cultural evening for all ages.

experiences.name: Waimea Valley Nature Walk and Waterfall Swim
experiences.description: Hike through a lush botanical garden along a well-maintained family-friendly trail leading to the stunning 45-foot Waimea Falls. Kids and adults can swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall (life jackets provided). The valley also features cultural demonstrations and ancient Hawaiian archaeological sites along the path.

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium Visit
experiences.description: Discover Hawaii's incredible marine life at one of the finest aquariums in the United States. Walk through an underwater tunnel surrounded by sharks, rays, and hundreds of tropical fish species. The center features interactive tide pools, turtle exhibits, and whale discovery centers that educate and entertain children and adults alike. A perfect rainy-day or mid-day activity.

experiences.name: Kailua Beach Kayaking and Sandbar Adventure
experiences.description: Paddle across the crystal-clear turquoise waters of Kailua Bay to the famous Flat Island sandbar and Popoia Island. Rent kayaks or join a guided family tour and enjoy one of Oahu's most beautiful and uncrowded beaches. The calm bay conditions make it ideal for children, and the white sand beach is perfect for building sandcastles and picnicking after your paddle.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Honolulu Airport. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in to your Beachfront suite. Enjoy a welcome amenity — chilled champagne, fresh tropical fruit platter, and a lei greeting from resort staff. Decompress on your private lanai listening to the ocean.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — order the fresh island fish tacos, macadamia-crusted chicken, and a tropical mocktail or cocktail to wind down after travel

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night — keep Day 1 completely relaxed. Confirm resort early check-in or luggage storage arrangements in advance. Request turndown service and a next-day wake-up call for a refreshed start to Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Spend the morning exploring the Aegean Bliss Resort grounds — relax on the beachfront, take a dip in the infinity pool, and let the family settle into island time. Light orientation walk along the resort's private beach stretch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hanauma Bay for the Snorkeling Experience. Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries as a family. Crystal-clear waters filled with sea turtles, vibrant reef fish, and colorful coral make this an unforgettable first full afternoon. Hire a private guide for a premium, personalized snorkeling session.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for sunset cocktails on the beachfront terrace. Enjoy a premium dinner at the resort's signature oceanfront restaurant — fresh catch of the day, Hawaiian poke bowls, and a curated wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant — full Hawaiian breakfast spread with fresh papaya, açaí bowls, eggs Benedict with kalua pork, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Light picnic-style lunch at Hanauma Bay — pre-arranged gourmet bento boxes with sushi, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature oceanfront restaurant — grilled opah (moonfish), lobster bisque, and mango cheesecake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations — book online well ahead of your trip. Arrive early for the best marine life activity. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the marine ecosystem. Children must be supervised in the water at all times.

day_by_day.morning: Kailua Beach Kayaking and Sandbar Adventure — depart early for the stunning turquoise waters of Kailua Bay. Paddle as a family across the bay to the famous Flat Island sandbar. Enjoy the calm, shallow waters perfect for all ages. Private guide included for safety and storytelling about the bay's history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-kayaking, relax on Kailua Beach — one of Hawaii's most beautiful stretches of white sand. Build sandcastles, wade in the calm surf, or simply soak up the afternoon sun under a private beach umbrella setup arranged by your concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort area. Enjoy dinner at a top-rated Honolulu fine dining restaurant — choose from renowned spots like Senia or MW Restaurant for a farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoothie bowls, Belgian waffles with lilikoi (passion fruit) syrup, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Kailua — gourmet sandwiches, fresh tropical juices, and shave ice from a premium local vendor
meals.dinner: Senia Restaurant, Honolulu — tasting menu featuring locally sourced Hawaiian ingredients, paired wines, and artisan desserts

day_by_day.notes: Kayak rentals and guided tours should be booked in advance, especially during peak August season. Apply waterproof sunscreen before kayaking. Kailua is approximately 30–40 minutes from most Waikiki-area resorts — arrange private transportation.

day_by_day.morning: Fly or ferry to Maui (short inter-island flight, approximately 35 minutes). Check into a premium day-use suite or lounge at a Maui luxury property for freshening up. Head straight to the Maui Ocean Center Aquarium for an immersive family experience — walk through the open-ocean tunnel, touch tide pools, and discover Hawaii's incredible marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming town of Lahaina — browse art galleries, pick up premium Hawaiian souvenirs, and stroll the historic waterfront. Visit the iconic Banyan Tree and learn about Lahaina's rich cultural and whaling history with a private local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Old Lahaina Luau — one of Hawaii's most authentic and celebrated luau experiences. Enjoy the traditional imu ceremony (underground pig roast), hula performances, fire knife dancing, and a lavish feast of Hawaiian dishes under the stars on the ocean's edge.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — continental spread with pastries, tropical fruits, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Lahaina waterfront dining — fresh fish tacos, clam chowder, and tropical cocktails at Fleetwood's on Front St.
meals.dinner: Old Lahaina Luau — full traditional Hawaiian feast including kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia (coconut pudding), and open bar

day_by_day.notes: Old Lahaina Luau is one of the most sought-after experiences in Hawaii — book tickets months in advance. Dress in resort casual or Hawaiian attire. The luau is family-friendly and highly recommended for all ages. Arrange round-trip private transportation between the aquarium, Lahaina town, and the luau venue.

day_by_day.morning: Full Maui day — Early morning Road to Hana private luxury tour. Depart at sunrise with a private driver-guide in a premium SUV. Stop at Twin Falls for a refreshing swim, Wai'anapanapa Black Sand Beach for stunning photos, and bamboo forest trailheads for short family walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana journey — stop at Oheo Gulch (Seven Sacred Pools) for a scenic overlook and light hiking. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by your private chef and served at a scenic ocean overlook. Head back toward Kaanapali or Wailea area.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at a Maui fine dining restaurant — Merriman's Maui in Kapalua offers breathtaking ocean views and farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine. Return to Honolulu via evening inter-island flight.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast from the resort — fresh fruit cups, granola bars, and premium coffee in travel cups
meals.lunch: Gourmet private picnic on the Road to Hana — charcuterie boards, fresh island fruit, artisan sandwiches, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Merriman's Maui — whole fresh fish, Maui cattle company filet mignon, and Maui Gold pineapple upside-down cake

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is a full-day commitment — start early. A private guided vehicle is strongly recommended over self-driving for comfort and safety on the winding roads. Keep younger children comfortable with snacks, entertainment, and frequent stops. Confirm return flight timing to allow ample buffer.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the resort's world-class spa — book family-friendly treatments such as Hawaiian lomi lomi massages, coconut scrubs, and hot stone therapy. Let the kids enjoy the resort's supervised kids' club while parents indulge in premium spa services.
day_by_day.afternoon: Waimea Valley Nature Walk and Waterfall Swim on Oahu's North Shore. Hike through a stunning botanical garden on a well-maintained, family-friendly trail leading to the beautiful Waimea Falls. Swim in the natural pool beneath the waterfall — a magical experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.evening: North Shore dining experience — enjoy a casual-yet-premium sunset dinner at Haleiwa Joe's Haiku Gardens or Ted's Bakery for legendary North Shore plates. Stroll through the charming surf town of Haleiwa before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort spa café — avocado toast, acai bowls, fresh-pressed green juices, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Waimea Valley café — light sandwiches, fresh tropical smoothies, and island snacks post-waterfall swim
meals.dinner: Haleiwa Joe's North Shore — fresh catch of the day, coconut shrimp, prime rib, and their famous hula pie dessert

day_by_day.notes: Waimea Valley requires life jackets for swimming at the falls — provided on-site. The trail is approximately 0.75 miles each way and suitable for all fitness levels. North Shore is about 45–60 minutes from Waikiki — arrange private transportation. Haleiwa town is worth extra time for browsing local shops and getting shave ice.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise catamaran sailing charter along Oahu's coastline. Watch the sun rise over Diamond Head from the water, spot sea turtles and spinner dolphins, and enjoy a catered breakfast on deck with fresh pastries, tropical fruit, and mimosas (juice for the kids).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Diamond Head State Monument — hike to the summit of this iconic volcanic crater for panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. The 1.6-mile round-trip trail is moderately easy and suitable for families. Arrange a private guide for historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's beachfront bar. Enjoy a premium dinner at a renowned Waikiki restaurant — Nobu Honolulu for world-class Japanese-Peruvian fusion cuisine in an elegant setting.

meals.breakfast: On-board catamaran breakfast — fresh pastries, tropical fruit platters, yogurt parfaits, and mimosas/juices
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch near Diamond Head — premium poke bowls and fresh coconut water at Ono Seafood or a curated delivery from a top local poke spot
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu — black cod miso, wagyu beef, yellowtail jalapeño, and signature Nobu desserts

day_by_day.notes: Private catamaran charters should be booked well in advance for August. Bring hats, sunscreen, and light layers for the morning sail. Diamond Head hike is best done in the afternoon after the morning crowds thin — bring plenty of water. Nobu Honolulu reservations are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour of Oahu — soar over the Ko'olau Mountains, Hanauma Bay from above, the Pali Lookout, and the stunning windward coastline. A thrilling and visually spectacular experience for the whole family that offers a completely new perspective of the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center — a world-class attraction where families can explore six Polynesian villages (Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and New Zealand), participate in cultural demonstrations, and learn traditional crafts like coconut husking, fire-making, and weaving.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Polynesian Cultural Center's Ha: Breath of Life evening show — a spectacular Broadway-style performance celebrating Polynesian culture, music, and dance. Enjoy the included Ali'i Luau dinner before the show.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant — eggs your way, Hawaiian sweet bread French toast, fresh tropical juices, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Polynesian Cultural Center — feast at the Gateway Bar & Grill with island-style plates, fresh fruit, and local favorites
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau at Polynesian Cultural Center — traditional Hawaiian feast with kalua pig, poi, fresh fish, tropical desserts, and cultural entertainment

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours require advance booking and weight/age restrictions apply — confirm details with the operator. The Polynesian Cultural Center is approximately 35 miles from Waikiki (about 1 hour drive) — arrange private transportation. The full PCC experience (afternoon + evening show) is a full day commitment and highly recommended for families.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private beach day at the resort — reserve a premium beachfront cabana with dedicated butler service. Enjoy watersports available through the resort (stand-up paddleboarding, boogie boarding, snorkeling gear rental). Let the kids play in the surf while adults relax in luxury.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium shopping excursion to Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's premier luxury shopping destination. Browse high-end boutiques including Louis Vuitton, Tiffany & Co., Chanel, and local Hawaiian designers. Pick up premium gifts, jewelry, and aloha wear to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-celebration dinner at one of Honolulu's finest restaurants — Alan Wong's Honolulu, a James Beard Award-winning chef's flagship restaurant celebrating Hawaii Regional Cuisine at its finest. Reflect on the trip's highlights over an extraordinary meal.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — order the resort's premium breakfast in bed package with fresh-squeezed juices, pastries, eggs, and Kona coffee served on your private lanai
meals.lunch: Ala Moana Center — dine at Mariposa at Neiman Marcus for an elegant lunch with stunning views and refined Hawaiian-inspired cuisine
meals.dinner: Alan Wong's Honolulu — chef's tasting menu featuring Hawaii Regional Cuisine with wine pairings; signature dishes include the 'Da Bag' clam chowder and ginger-crusted onaga

day_by_day.notes: Reserve the resort cabana and butler service the day before. Alan Wong's reservations are highly competitive — book as far in advance as possible. Consider scheduling a private shopping assistant or stylist at Ala Moana for a truly premium retail experience. This is a wonderful day to purchase any last-minute keepsakes.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk along the resort's private beachfront — take in the last moments of the Hawaiian sunrise, collect shells, and soak in the peaceful atmosphere. Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast at the resort. Pack and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout (confirm with resort — luxury properties often accommodate late checkout requests). Spend remaining time at the resort pool or spa. Private luxury transfer to Honolulu International Airport. Arrive with ample time for premium/first-class check-in and lounge access.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight — carry the memories of 10 extraordinary days in Hawaii. Enjoy airport lounge amenities before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — go all out with a full spread including fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, loco moco (Hawaiian breakfast classic), and a final cup of Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Resort light lunch or airport lounge dining — fresh salads, sandwiches, and tropical beverages
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport restaurant — Daniel K. Inouye International Airport has several dining options for a final taste of Hawaii

day_by_day.notes: Request late checkout from Aegean Bliss Resort at the beginning of your stay to secure availability. Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international or mainland departures. Consider purchasing premium Hawaiian gifts at the airport — Honolulu airport has excellent local vendors including Longs Drugs for famous chocolate-covered macadamia nuts and local treats.
